subject.title: Crestodian chat hijacks natural language into operations; approvals require a literal hardcoded yes

question: Should Crestodian normal chat become strictly AI-first, with deterministic parsing limited to exact typed commands and rescue/no-model fallback?
rationale: The source supports real bugs, but the requested endpoint changes setup UX, fallback semantics, approval intent, and executor shape across CLI, Gateway, and rescue surfaces, so maintainer intent should set the boundary before implementation.

options.title: Adopt AI-first boundary
options.body: Make normal chat route natural language to the agent/planner, keep only anchored typed commands deterministic, and repair approval, stale-proposal, redaction, and Gemini parity together.

options.title: Ship parser safety first
options.body: Anchor the most dangerous deterministic command regexes and broaden literal approval handling while leaving the broader AI-first and executor refactor work for follow-up.

options.title: Split the umbrella
options.body: Keep this as the canonical issue but require smaller follow-ups for parser safety, approval intent, stale proposals, secret redaction, executor refactor, and Gemini parity.

recommendation.title: Adopt AI-first boundary
recommendation.body: Make normal chat route natural language to the agent/planner, keep only anchored typed commands deterministic, and repair approval, stale-proposal, redaction, and Gemini parity together.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant Crestodian feature history and current issue ownership both point to steipete as the best available product-boundary owner.
